extraction.name: SeamlessAlign
extraction.description: A multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations of more than 470,000 hours across 37 languages, created using parallel data mining in a joint multimodal embedding space (SONAR) and speech-language identification.
extraction.creator: Meta AI
extraction.citeAs: Seamless Communication et al. SeamlessM4T: Massively Multilingual & Multimodal Machine Translation. arXiv:2308.11596, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Starting with 4 million hours of raw audio from a publicly available repository of crawled web data and sentence-segmented text from NLLB, audio files were chunked into overlapping segments using Voice Activity Detection (VAD) and over-segmentation. Audio and text corpora were projected into a shared SONAR multimodal embedding space, followed by global parallel mining using FAISS similarity search and margin-based scoring.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: In evaluation data (CVSS-C), some samples were missing in 8 out of 21 languages (Catalan, German, Estonian, French, Italian, Mongolian, Persian, and Portuguese).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data, and sentence-segmented text drawn from NLLB.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were deduplicated by URLs, downloaded, resampled to 16kHz, filtered for non-speech using an audio event detection (AED) model, segmented using Silero VAD, and over-segmented with overlapping splits. Target discrete acoustic units for speech were extracted via XLS-R-1B and k-means clustering.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Length filtering was applied to remove utterances shorter than 0.1 seconds or longer than 50 seconds, pairs with skewed text-to-audio ratio exceeding 5 sub-words per second, texts longer than 250 sub-words, texts containing more than 20% emojis, more than 50% punctuation, or more than 50% spaces, and pairs with toxicity imbalance exceeding an imbalance threshold of 1.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Parallel alignments were automatically mined using a margin-based nearest-neighbor score (with k=16) in the SONAR embedding space with a margin threshold of 1.15. For speech targets, discrete acoustic units were extracted via k-means clustering (K=10,000) on features from XLS-R-1B, and text transcriptions were generated using an in-house ASR model. Human evaluations used the XSTS protocol (semantic similarity rated 1 to 5) and the MOS protocol (Likert scale 1 to 5 for clarity, sound quality, and naturalness).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: In XSTS human evaluation, each item was evaluated by 3 annotators (up to 30 per language pair). If annotators disagreed by 2 or more score points, 2 additional annotators scored the item (total of 5). The median score across annotators was used, and scores were calibrated using an English monolingual cross-lingual calibration set with moderated calibration to reduce annotator bias.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 to 5 annotators per item for XSTS evaluation
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Team members who were aware of the toxic nature of samples were used for human evaluation of detected toxicity; external vendor annotators were used for translation evaluation (XSTS and MOS).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ECAPA-TDNN for speech language identification, Silero VAD for voice activity detection, Audio Event Detection (AED) model, FAISS for GPU nearest neighbor search, SONAR encoders and decoders, ETOX with Toxicity-200 word lists for toxicity filtering and detection, XLS-R-1B for discrete acoustic unit extraction, and an in-house ASR model for transcription generation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Code, model weights, inference code, finetuning recipes, and metadata to recreate the unfiltered 470,000 hours of SeamlessAlign are open-sourced at https://github.com/facebookresearch/seamless_communication, with code issues tracked via GitHub.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The training data was mined from publicly available web sources; despite heavy data cleaning, personally identifiable information (PII) may not be entirely eliminated. Evaluations also assessed demographic attributes including gender, race/ethnicity, religion, age, and sexual orientation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aimed at lowering cross-lingual communication barriers, enhancing global connectivity, and promoting digital inclusion and accessibility for people with low literacy, visual impairments, or whose languages lack standardized writing systems. Downstream risks include potential misuse by bad actors for scams or misinformation targeting low-digital-literacy groups.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Gender representation analysis showed masculine lexica are predominant in the mined and evaluation datasets. When source inputs lack gender clues, models exhibit an average preference of ~10% toward masculine translations, and show ~3% lower translation quality when translating from feminine source forms into English. Toxic terms also concentrate heavily on certain demographic axes depending on the language.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: SeamlessM4T is a research model not intended for production deployment, certified translations, or domain-specific use (e.g., medical or legal). It was trained on short inputs; translating longer sequences may degrade quality or result in truncations and omissions. Word-list-based toxicity filtering suffers from false positives and false negatives, and lexical gender tracking is limited by relying on a fixed set of English nouns.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Multimodal and multilingual machine translation research, speech-to-speech translation (S2ST), speech-to-text translation (S2TT), text-to-speech translation (T2ST), text-to-text translation (T2TT), and automatic speech recognition (ASR).
